title: pvTransform
body:
## pvTransform

Applies a translation, rotation and scaling (Transform, ParaView default the Transform3 'Transform' choice, identity until set) to point coordinates. Point-set inputs keep their type; image and rectilinear inputs come out as structured grids. Vectors and normals are rotated with the geometry and, with TransformAllInputVectors (ParaView default true), every other 3-component array too. The curated transform is the simpler alternative.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- With TransformAllInputVectors true, 3-component arrays that are not vectors (e.g. RGB colours or principal values) are rotated as well; turn it off in that case.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `Transform`. Identity: `filters/TransformFilter`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Transform filter. Accepted data: explicit-point datasets (polygonal, unstructured or structured grids) (vtkPointSet); image data (uniform rectilinear grids) (vtkImageData); rectilinear grids (vtkRectilinearGrid). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPointSet","vtkImageData","vtkRectilinearGrid"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Transform` | The values in this property allow you to specify the transform (translation, rotation, and scaling) to apply to the input dataset. | `{"type":"typed proxy","choices":["GeoTransform","RotateAroundOriginTransform","Transform"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `{"type":"Transform"}` |
| `TransformAllInputVectors` | If off, only Vectors and Normals will be transformed. If on, all three-component data arrays (considered as 3D vectors) will be transformed. All other arrays won't be flipped and will only be copied. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |

### Nested `Transform` → `GeoTransform`

Syntax: `{"type":"GeoTransform","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `transforms/GeoTransform`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Transform.options.DestinationProjection` | PROJ definition of the output coordinates, e.g. “+proj=utm +zone=33 +datum=WGS84” for UTM eastings and northings in metres, or “+proj=cart +datum=WGS84” for geocentric x, y, z. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Transform.options.SourceProjection` | PROJ definition of the coordinates the input points are in, e.g. “+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84” for longitude and latitude in degrees (x = longitude, y = latitude). | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Transform.options.TransformZCoordinate` | When true, x, y and z are converted together through PROJ’s CRS-to-CRS transformation (needed for 3D conversions such as geographic to geocentric); when false, only x and y are converted and z is left unchanged, which suits elevations kept in their own units. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |

### Nested `Transform` → `RotateAroundOriginTransform`

Syntax: `{"type":"RotateAroundOriginTransform","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `extended_sources/RotateAroundOriginTransform`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Transform.options.Originofrotation` | Pivot point [x, y, z] that stays fixed while the dataset rotates around it. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `Transform.options.Rotate` | Rotation angles [rx, ry, rz] about axes through OriginOfRotation parallel to x, y and z, combined in VTK’s Z-X-Y convention (the matrix is RotateZ · RotateX · RotateY); for a rotation about a single axis the order does not matter. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |

### Nested `Transform` → `Transform`

Syntax: `{"type":"Transform","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `extended_sources/Transform3`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Transform.options.Rotate` | Rotation angles [rx, ry, rz] about the x, y and z axes through the coordinate origin, combined in VTK’s Z-X-Y convention (the matrix is RotateZ · RotateX · RotateY); for a rotation about a single axis the order does not matter. Applied after Scale and before Translate. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `Transform.options.Scale` | Scale factors [sx, sy, sz] along x, y and z about the coordinate origin, applied first. Values above 1 enlarge, below 1 shrink, and negative values mirror the geometry. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `Transform.options.Translate` | Displacement [tx, ty, tz] added to every point after scaling and rotation. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvTransform",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
